Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ipw (development version)

Bug fixes

  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm(): offset() terms in the numerator and denominator formulas were silently dropped, so the models were fitted without the offset and the weights were wrong. This affected ipw 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 on CRAN; ipw 1.2.1.1 was fine. Formulas are now used as written.
  • ipwpoint(): denominator = ~ . (all other columns of data) failed with “Variables not found in data: .” and works again, as in ipw 1.2.1.1. In ipwtm() a . is now a clear error, because it would include the id, time and exposure columns; list the covariates instead.
  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm(), family = "ordinal": an unordered factor exposure whose levels are not numbers now gives a warning, because its levels are used in alphabetical order unless set otherwise (e.g. “high” < “low” < “mid”). Use an ordered factor to make the order explicit.
  • ipwtm(), family = "survival": a ties argument passed through ... to coxph() was silently ignored (Efron was always used), and method gave the error “formal argument matched by multiple actual arguments”. Both are now passed on; the default is still ties = "efron".
  • ipwtm(), family = "survival": rows with tstart >= timevar now give a clear error instead of “missing values in object” or no error at all.
  • Clearer errors: ipwpoint() with family = "gaussian" and a non-numeric exposure (was “NA/NaN/Inf in ‘y’”); ipwplot() with missing weights (was “‘x’ contains missing values”) or a binwidth of length > 1.
  • ipwtm(), family = "survival", type = "first" or "cens": the probability of each row now uses the baseline hazard over the row’s own interval (tstart, timevar]. Before, it used the increase in the baseline hazard since the previous time point in the whole data set, which is only right when all subjects share one time grid (as in haartdat). Weights change for data in which subjects have their own follow-up times; for data with a common time grid they are unchanged. type = "all" was not affected.
  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm(): a binomial (or survival) 0/1 exposure stored as a factor or character is now used by its labels. With factor levels in the order c("1", "0") the probabilities of the two exposure values were swapped, giving wrong weights.
  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm(), family = "ordinal": a character exposure is now an error. It was ordered alphabetically (e.g. “high” < “low” < “mid”). Use an ordered factor or numeric codes.
  • ipwtm(): a covariate called selvar was replaced by the internal selection indicator; it is now used as the user’s covariate.
  • ipwtm(): duplicated combinations of id and timevar are now an error (as in ipwprobtm()).
  • ipwpoint(): an exposure that takes only one value is now an error instead of returning meaningless weights.
  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm(): infinite values in model variables now give an error that names the variables.
  • ipwprobtm(): den and num larger than 1 are now an error.
  • tstartfun(): warns when follow-up times are <= -1, because the starting time of -1 given to the first record is then not before the follow-up time.
  • ipwplot(): zero or negative weights with logscale = TRUE are now an error; they were silently left out of the plot.
  • ipwtm() examples: the cluster bootstrap moved to vignette("ipw") (section 5), and the part of Example 2 that needs nlme (in Suggests) only runs when nlme is installed.

Documentation

  • New article “Bugs fixed after ipw 1.3.2” on the package website: for each bug above, an example run in ipw 1.2.1.1, ipw 1.3.2 and this version, with the weights compared with weights computed by hand.

New features

  • ipwtm(): type = "all" now works for family = "multinomial" and "ordinal" (time-varying categorical exposures that switch back and forth).
  • ipwtm(): type = "all" now works for family = "survival", following Graffeo, Latouche, Geskus & Chevret (2018, Biometrical Journal): exposure events may recur, an Andersen-Gill Cox model is fitted on all rows, and each row’s probability uses the cumulative baseline hazard over its own interval.
  • New ipwprobtm(): time-varying inverse probability weights from probabilities you estimated yourself (for example with machine learning or SuperLearner): the ratios are multiplied over time within each subject, in time order. For a point treatment no function is needed: the weights are num / den.
  • ipwpoint(): new families for count exposures ("poisson", "negbin") and skewed continuous exposures ("gamma", "lognormal").
  • Smooth terms (s(), te(), ti(), t2()) in model formulas are fitted as generalized additive models with mgcv: in ipwpoint() for the binomial, gaussian and poisson families, and in ipwtm() for the binomial family.
  • ipwpoint(): new estimand argument for a binomial exposure: "ATE" (default), "ATT" (effect in the treated) and "ATO" (overlap weights).
  • Existing calls are unchanged: without smooth terms the models are still fitted with glm(), and estimand defaults to "ATE". A covariate named s, te, ti or t2 is treated as an ordinary variable.

Documentation

  • New vignette, “Inverse probability weighting with ipw” (vignette("ipw")), covering every function, with the new models highlighted. Its standard-errors section describes, from the package’s simulation study, when the bootstrap helps (well-behaved weights) and when no standard error is reliable (extreme weights).
  • Bootstrap standard errors. The help pages of ipwpoint() and ipwtm() have a new “Standard errors” paragraph in Details. ?ipwpoint has a bootstrap example that re-estimates the weights and the marginal structural model in each bootstrap sample; the cluster bootstrap that resamples patients and re-runs both ipwtm() calls for the HAART example is in section 5 of vignette("ipw"). Robust standard errors (svyglm(), cluster()) treat the weights as known. They were conservative for a binary point treatment with good overlap, but can be too small for a continuous exposure and for time-varying weights; Austin (2016, doi:10.1002/sim.7084) recommends the bootstrap.
  • ipwplot(): the help page now documents the return value (NULL, invisibly).
  • The ipwtm() examples no longer call graphics.off(), which closed all of the user’s open graphics devices.

License

  • License changed back to GPL (>= 2), the license of ipw before version 1.3.0.

ipw 1.3.2

CRAN release: 2026-11-01

Bug fixes

  • ipwpoint(): weights.trunc was wrong whenever trunc was set. The lower and upper quantiles were recycled across rows, so every truncated weight was replaced by one of the two bounds. Weights are now clipped at the trunc and 1 - trunc quantiles, and weights between the bounds are left unchanged.
  • ipwtm() with family = "multinomial" or "ordinal": predicted probabilities are now matched to the observed exposure by level name rather than by column position. 1.3.1 stopped with an error for a two-level exposure, or when an exposure level did not occur among the rows used to fit the models.
  • ipwpoint() with family = "multinomial" now works for a two-level exposure; 1.3.1 stopped with an error (“Observed exposure levels do not match fitted probability levels”).
  • Added a test for unstabilized weights (no numerator) with family = "multinomial" and "ordinal" in ipwpoint(). These failed in 1.3.0 and were fixed by the 1.3.1 rewrite (#3, @adcascone).
  • ipwtm() with type = "first" and family = "multinomial" / "ordinal": a switch is again defined as the first record at any level other than the lowest level in the whole data set, as in ipw <= 1.2.1.1. In 1.3.1 the reference level was chosen separately for each subject.

Improvements

  • ipwtm() now checks that all model variables exist and contain no missing values, and that a binomial/survival exposure is coded 0/1, with clear error messages instead of errors from inside glm() / coxph().
  • ipwtm() with family = "survival" now stops with a clear message when a formula contains strata(), which is not supported.
  • Fitted models returned in num.mod / den.mod no longer carry an inlined copy of the data in their call, so printing them is readable again.
  • ipwpoint() and ipwtm() share one set of internal helpers for argument checks, formula construction, probability extraction and truncation.
  • Removed blanket import() of whole packages; all calls use pkg::fun. methods is no longer imported.

Tests

  • Test suite expanded: exact checks of truncation, row-order invariance, two-level multinomial vs binomial equivalence, and error messages.
  • New regression test against ipw 1.2.1.1 (reference weights created with data-raw/make-regression-fixtures.R).

ipw 1.3.1

CRAN release: 2026-10-30

  • Core Refactoring (ipwtm, ipwpoint, ipwplot, tstartfun):
    • Improved defensive input validation, parameter checking, and error messages across all core functions.
    • Modernized formula construction (as.formula()) to eliminate fragile eval(parse(text = ...)) string manipulations.
    • Fixed variable symbol evaluation issues when passing variables as function arguments rather than raw names.
    • Modularized ipwtm into dedicated family modeling engines (binomial, survival, multinomial, ordinal, gaussian).
    • Replaced manual survival hazard step-differencing with continuous baseline hazard interpolation using survival::basehaz and stats::approx.
    • Refactored tstartfun to use safe column evaluation and direct vector lag logic (c(-1, t[-length(t)])).
  • Test Suite Expansion:
    • Upgraded testthat suite to 3rd edition specs, expanding coverage for multinomial, ordinal, gaussian, unstabilized models, weight truncation, and invalid parameter rejection.

ipw 1.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-01-27

  • New maintainer: Hung Thai Tran.
  • License changed to MIT (earlier versions: GPL (>= 2)).
